decisions.note: Maker framed label-browsing as secondary/backup to search; client rejected this, insisting both be first-class (protects REF-BM-11 as a co-equal item).
Client demanded auto-fetched title/description before the maker's goal recap had surfaced it.
First save prototype had no tagging step; client asked to add labels while saving.
Client raised re-save/duplicate-url handling before the maker had addressed it.
Auto-collect only grabbed title/description; client asked for favicon and preview image too.
Of three tagging-UI styles offered (comma text / typeahead pills / tap-to-pick), client chose the typeahead style, the only one truly fulfilling REF-BM-10's autocomplete requirement.
Chosen style allowed case-variant duplicate tags ("Recipes" vs "recipes"); client required case-insensitive canonicalization to one tag.
Search covered only title/description/url/tags; client (and maker's own honest flag) established a dedicated notes field with full-text coverage.
Find prototype only supported AND narrowing; client asked for OR ("any of these") and NOT ("exclude") combination too.
Maker had clicking a card open the editor; client corrected it — click must navigate to the original url, editing moved to a separate pencil control.
Only permanent delete existed; client asked for a reversible "set aside" distinct from permanent delete.
No unread/read-later concept existed yet; client asked for a distinct "haven't read this" list separate from set-aside.
Proposed mechanism auto-marked items read on visit; client corrected this — only an explicit "Mark read" action should clear unread status.
Initial bulk-action bar lacked "mark to-read" (reverse) and "remove label", both implied by REF-BM-20's bulk action list.
No way to select all bookmarks matching the current filter; client requested it to fulfil "apply to whole filtered collection".
Maker defaulted to requiring a title to save; client corrected that only the url should be required.
Page-snapshot preservation was entirely absent from the design; client raised it unprompted as the feature closest to their original goal.
Bulk import of existing bookmarks had never been discussed; client raised it as essential for day one.
Saved filter combinations (bundles) had never been discussed; client requested reusable saved views.
Import design hadn't addressed preserving original save dates; client asked, matching REF-BM-30's "preserving...date added".
Saved-view demo only exercised labels; client asked whether a typed search term is also captured, per the Bundle entity's search-term field.

Client and maker settled on a 'readable copy' (extracted text/photo) instead of the reference's literal local-HTML-snapshot approach; both affirmed it without flagging the deviation from REF-BM-24's spec.
